title: Compact incident fact sheet + verification kit (customer-facing draft)
body:
Compact Incident Fact Sheet + Verification Kit (customer-facing draft)

Purpose
A short, actionable customer-facing summary of the outage with an attached verification kit customers can use to validate claims about request routing, timestamps, and observed errors. Designed for regulated customers and partners that require reproducible evidence and a concise remediation plan.

Executive summary
On 2027-09-20 (UTC), between 03:18 and 04:12 UTC, a routing regression in our regional model-router caused a subset of requests from eu-west-1 to be routed to a legacy inference pool that had an incompatible soft-config for structured streaming. Customers experienced elevated latency and truncated streaming responses (partial chunks) for approximately 54 minutes. No customer data was exfiltrated. We acknowledge the disruption and offer this compact kit so customers or auditors can independently verify the timeline and the remediation steps we performed.

Scope and impact
- Affected tenants: ~0.8% of active tenants routed through eu-west-1 during the window (identified by tenant routing tag).
- Affected APIs: streaming generation and streaming chat endpoints that rely on the structured output feature flag. Non-streaming generation and embeddings unaffected.
- Observable symptoms: increased 95th/99th percentile tail latency, truncated or prematurely ended stream events, some duplicate final tokens when clients retried.

High-level root cause (short)
A recent canary rollout changed the route selector priority order. Under a narrow condition (rolling config refresh + concurrent cache eviction), requests were matched to legacy pool IDs that were missing the structured streaming handshake extension, leading to early stream termination.

Timeline (all times UTC)
- 03:16:42 — config rollout start (canary batch 2)
- 03:17:05 — regional router refresh begins
- 03:18:09 — first customer-reported elevated latency (internal alert)
- 03:18:25 — engineering on-call engaged
- 03:21:40 — spike in stream termination errors detected by observability (rule: stream-terminate-rate > 3x baseline)
- 03:34:12 — automated rollback of canary batch 2 initiated
- 03:36:00 — routing revert complete in eu-west-1
- 03:36:30 — initial reductions in error rates observed
- 04:12:10 — system stabilized and metrics returned to baseline

Verification kit contents (for customers/auditors)
1) Timeline bundle (logs): consolidated request logs (redacted PII) for eu-west-1 between 03:00 — 04:30 UTC. Each log block includes request_id, tenant_id_pseudonym, route_selector_snapshot, pool_id, and status.

2) Signed audit manifest: SHA256 hashes of log files and a signature using our incident key. Use the manifest to confirm file integrity.
   - logs_euw_0300-0430.jsonl.gz SHA256: 9f2c7b3a2c0f9d1d3b9e8a5f1c7bb2e6a2d5f3c8b1e6a7a6b8c2d4f3a0b1c2d
   - manifest_20270920.sig SHA256: e3a5b7f1c6d4e5f8a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a4b5c6d7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f

3) Repro scripts: small scripts (python) that take our logs and produce the same observability metrics we show in the public dashboard (95th/99th latencies, stream-terminate-rate). Scripts require only the gzipped jsonl log bundle and run locally.

4) Router snapshot diff: the canary vs baseline route selector config diff (human readable). This shows the priority change that led to fallback to legacy pools.

How to verify (recommended steps for customers)
- Step 1: Download logs_euw_0300-0430.jsonl.gz and manifest_20270920.sig from the attachment link in the support ticket.
- Step 2: Validate file integrity: run shasum -a 256 on the downloaded files and compare to the manifest hashes above. Verify signature using the public incident key we publish on our trust page.
- Step 3: Run the included reproduce_metrics.py script against the log bundle. Confirm the reproduced spike in stream-terminate-rate and latency percentiles align with the values quoted below (tolerance: ±5%).
- Step 4: Inspect route_selector_snapshot field for requests with status=stream_terminated to confirm they were assigned legacy_pool_xx between 03:18:09 and 03:36:00.

Key observed metric snapshots (what customers will reproduce)
- stream-terminate-rate (requests/min) baseline: 2.1 — peak during window: 14.6 — post-rollback: 2.4
- p95 latency (ms) baseline: 230 — peak: 1,240 — post-rollback: 245
- p99 latency (ms) baseline: 620 — peak: 3,800 — post-rollback: 640

Actions we took (immediate)
- 03:34:12 — rolled back canary batch that introduced the selector change; verified rollback propagation to edge routers.
- 03:35:00 — disabled structured-streaming handshake fallback for legacy pools to prevent mismatch in future transitions.
- 03:40:00 — increased realtime observability thresholds and created an automated circuit that pauses route rollouts if stream-terminate-rate > 5x baseline for more than 2 minutes.

Longer-term mitigations planned
- Add automated integration test that exercises structured-streaming handshake during canary rollouts (target: Q4 2027).
- Improve route-selector unit tests and add a canary-stage integration harness to reject selectors that route to pools missing handshake metadata.
- Post-deployment: 90-day audit of rollout policies and associated circuit-breakers; share summary with affected customers.

Customer recommended actions
- If you saw incomplete streaming responses, we recommend replaying requests using the request_id list we will attach to your tenant support case. The replay tool can be found in the reproduce_scripts folder and includes a safe-mode toggle to avoid double-side effects.
- If you require a signed attestation for compliance, reply to this support thread and we will provide a scoped attestation document for your tenant.

SLA and credits
- We consider this an eligible incident for service credits under Section 4.2 of the SLA (regional routing errors resulting in sustained SLO breaches). We will open a credit case for impacted tenants automatically; the expected timeline for credit application is 7–10 business days.

FAQ (short)
Q: Was customer data exposed?
A: No. The error mode caused stream termination and truncated outputs, not data exfiltration. Logs provided are redacted; full sensitive fields are removed or pseudonymized.

Q: Can this happen in other regions?
A: The root cause was a selector priority change combined with a localized cache eviction. We have applied the temporary hardening to all regions and will roll permanent fixes globally after verification.

Contact & escalation
- Primary CS contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai)
- Engineering lead: Markus Chen (markus@redwood.ai)
- If you need legal/compliance attestation: compliance@redwood.ai
- For urgent cross-tenant audit requests, contact support and reference "INC-4321 - verification kit request".

Appendix (technical artifacts and sample commands)
- Validate manifest: shasum -a 256 logs_euw_0300-0430.jsonl.gz
- Verify signature: ./verify_manifest.sh manifest_20270920.sig public_incident_key.pem
- Reproduce metrics: python reproduce_metrics.py --input logs_euw_0300-0430.jsonl.gz --output observed_metrics.csv

Notes and open questions (internal use but visible to customers in this draft)
- We are correlating router cache eviction logs with the rollout window; final analysis may shift the precise sequence by a few seconds.
- We will update hashes if further redaction is required for tenant-specific replays.

End of compact fact sheet and verification kit.

Document status: draft for customer review; expected to be published to status page once the manifest signature and attachments are uploaded to the secure customer portal.
